title: BalancerPoolerV2 sandwich via user-controlled minBptAmountOut
description: `dispatch` accepts `minBptAmountOut` from caller-supplied `extraData`, defaulting to 0 when empty. NFTMinterV2.mint forwards whatever extraData the caller passes. The protocol-owned BPT output (held at BalancerPoolerV2 for later owner withdrawal via withdrawBPT) is thus unprotected against sandwich/slippage. An attacker can (a) self-sandwich — flash-loan the prime token, imbalance the pool, call mint() themselves with minBptAmountOut=0, rebalance for arbitrage profit — or (b) frontrun a legitimate minter. In both cases the protocol receives materially fewer BPT than a fair add-liquidity would produce.
impact: Direct reduction of protocol BPT treasury. Withdrawable owner funds are permanently diminished each time an attack occurs.
attack_path: Performs unbalanced swap on the target Balancer V3 pool, saturating it with primeToken.
Calls NFTMinterV2.mint targeting the BalancerPoolerV2 index with `extraData=""` (minBptAmountOut=0).
Protocol's single-sided unbalanced join returns depressed BPT.
Attacker swaps back and repays flashloan, netting arbitrage profit.
recommendation: Remove user-supplied `minBptAmountOut`; instead enforce an owner-configured floor derived from a TWAP or a minimum BPT-per-primeToken ratio. Optionally restrict dispatch callers to a paused-aware context.
